driedApricots.name: Dried Apricots
driedApricots.description: High in vitamin A, vitamin C, iron and potassium, which support the heart and blood vessels. They also aid digestion.

raisins.name: Raisins
raisins.description: Grapes dried the natural way. Prized for their sweetness, their goodness and how well they keep.

prunes.name: Prunes (Dried Plums)
prunes.description: Sweet and full-flavoured, served with tea and used throughout cooking and confectionery. They keep for a long time, so they are easy to stock.

walnuts.name: Walnuts
walnuts.description: Walnuts carry protein, nourishing fatty acids, potassium, magnesium, iron and vitamin E. They support memory and help build immunity.

peanuts.name: Peanuts
peanuts.description: Rich in protein, healthy fatty acids, potassium, magnesium and B vitamins. They give the body energy and strengthen the immune system.

mungBeans.name: Mung Beans
mungBeans.description: Rich in protein, fibre, iron, magnesium and B vitamins. They aid digestion, give energy and suit light, dietary cooking.

beans.name: Beans
beans.description: Common beans, dried and cleaned for cooking. A staple pulse — high in plant protein, fibre and iron, and stable in storage for years.

apricotKernels.name: Apricot Kernels
apricotKernels.description: The kernel from inside the apricot stone. Rich in healthy fats and protein, used in confectionery and baking, and pressed for oil.

driedPeppers.name: Dried Peppers
driedPeppers.description: Capsicum dried whole in the sun. Used for spice blends, sauces and pickling, with the heat and colour concentrated by drying.

driedMelon.name: Dried Melon
driedMelon.description: Fergana melon cut into strips and sun-dried. Intensely sweet and fragrant — a Central Asian speciality served with tea.

compoteMix.name: Dried Fruit Compote Mix
compoteMix.description: A ready blend of dried apples, apricots, plums, cherries and berries for compote. Sold as a single line, so there is nothing to assemble.

sourCherries.name: Sour Cherries
sourCherries.description: Tart cherries dried whole. High in anthocyanins, and the acidity holds up in baking, confectionery and compote.

driedApples.name: Dried Apples
driedApples.description: Apples cut into rings and dried. Light, fibrous and easy to store — used for compote, muesli and snacking.

certification.sectionSubtitle: Registered with China's General Administration of Customs
certification.gaccBody: “KOKAND DRY FRUITS” LLC is listed in the GACC register of approved overseas food producers. That listing is what lets our product clear Chinese customs under our own registration rather than a trader's.
certification.coveredNote: The GACC listing covers dried apricots (HS 0813 10) and dried plums and cherries (HS 0813 20). Our other lines ship to markets where this registration is not required.

story.title: In this business since 2020
story.p1: a family-run producer and exporter of dried fruit, nuts and pulses in the Fergana Valley.
story.p2: “KOKAND DRY FRUITS” LLC works out of Kichik Oqmasjid in the Kokand district of Fergana Region, with a production capacity of 250 tonnes a year. Prunes, mung beans and dried apricots account for most of that volume; raisins, walnuts and peanuts are produced in smaller quantities.

driedApricots.intro: Apricots are laid out to dry within hours of picking, so the sugars concentrate without the fruit ever being stewed. We sort by colour and size across six grades — red, yellow, sugared, Limonka, natural and cut — and we do not use dye.

benefits.title: Vitamin A and potassium
benefits.text: The orange pigment is beta-carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A. Apricots also carry potassium and iron, which is why they are sold as a heart and circulation food.

benefits.title: Colour grading you can rely on
benefits.text: Lots are separated by shade and size before packing, so a shipment of light fruit stays light. You get the grade you bought, crate after crate.

benefits.title: Covered by our GACC listing
benefits.text: Dried apricots fall under HS 0813 10, one of the two codes our GACC registration covers, so this line enters China under our own registration.

raisins.tagline: Grapes dried the way they always have been
raisins.intro: Our raisins come from Fergana Valley vineyards and are sun-dried in the traditional way. We run five grades — Malayar, Sultana, Natural, Crimson and Jumbo Golden — which differ in size, colour and price rather than in processing.

benefits.title: Natural sugars, no additives
benefits.text: Nothing is added and nothing is coated. The sweetness is the grape's own, concentrated by drying rather than by syrup.

benefits.title: Five distinct grades
benefits.text: Malayar, Sultana, Natural, Crimson and Jumbo Golden — each with its own size, colour and price point.

benefits.title: Keeps and travels well
benefits.text: At 17% moisture or less, raisins ship without refrigeration and hold their softness for a year in sealed cartons.

prunes.intro: Plums are dried whole and slowly, which is what gives prunes their dark colour and their depth of flavour. We supply them with the stone in or pitted, calibrated by the number of pieces per kilogram so you know exactly what arrives.

benefits.title: Fibre and sorbitol
benefits.text: Prunes are one of the best-known digestive foods, and the reason is real: soluble fibre plus naturally occurring sorbitol.

benefits.title: Counted, not estimated
benefits.text: Calibration is by pieces per kilogram — 70/80, 80/90, 90/100 — so portioning and packing downstream stays predictable.

benefits.title: Our largest line, and GACC covered
benefits.text: Prunes carry the biggest share of our 250 tonnes a year, and HS 0813 20 is covered by our GACC registration for China.

walnuts.tagline: Kernels graded by size and colour
walnuts.intro: Walnuts are cracked and graded to halves, quarters, large and small pieces, and granulate. Colour is what sets the price in this trade, so kernels are separated by shade and then hand-checked before they are packed.

benefits.title: Omega-3 and vitamin E
benefits.text: Walnuts carry more alpha-linolenic acid than any other common nut, along with vitamin E, magnesium and protein.

benefits.title: Light halves, properly sorted
benefits.text: Light-coloured halves command the premium. Ours are separated by colour and checked by hand, so the grade holds across the lot.

benefits.title: Vacuum packing on request
benefits.text: Kernels oxidise faster than dried fruit. Vacuum or gas-flushed packing keeps them fresh through a long sea voyage.

peanuts.intro: We supply peanuts in shell and as cleaned kernels. Calibration follows the usual count-per-ounce grades, and lots ship with the certificates your destination market requires.

benefits.title: Protein at a working price
benefits.text: Around a quarter protein by weight, with potassium, magnesium and B vitamins — the reason peanuts anchor so many snack and confectionery lines.

benefits.title: Tested to your protocol
benefits.text: Aflatoxin limits differ by destination market. Tell us the protocol and the limit your import requires and we ship against that certificate.

benefits.title: Processed to your brief
benefits.text: Shelling and further processing are done to order, so you can take the kernel at whatever stage suits your line.

mungBeans.tagline: A pulse that moves in volume
mungBeans.intro: Mung beans are cleaned, calibrated and packed to a single standard grade. They are a staple across South and East Asia, and they are one of the three lines that carry the bulk of our annual volume.

benefits.title: Protein and fibre
benefits.text: High in plant protein, fibre, iron and magnesium, and light enough to sit in dietary and hospital cooking.

benefits.title: One of our main volumes
benefits.text: Along with prunes and dried apricots, mung beans account for most of the 250 tonnes we produce each year, so quantity is rarely the constraint.

benefits.title: Two-year shelf life
benefits.text: Dry pulses outlast dried fruit comfortably. Stored properly, mung beans hold for twenty-four months.

beans.tagline: A pulse that stores and travels
beans.intro: Common beans, dried and cleaned to food grade. They are one of the steadiest lines we run — no cold chain, no narrow seasonal window on the buying side, and a shelf life measured in years rather than months.

benefits.title: Protein and fibre
benefits.text: Around a fifth protein by weight, with fibre, iron, folate and potassium. The reason pulses anchor so much of the world's everyday cooking.

benefits.title: Cleaned and calibrated
benefits.text: Stones, splits and discoloured grain are taken out before packing, so what arrives is what you can cook without re-sorting.

benefits.title: Long, undemanding shelf life
benefits.text: Dry pulses need nothing but a cool, dry store. No refrigeration, no controlled atmosphere, and no seasonal rush to move stock.

apricotKernels.intro: When apricots are pitted for drying, the stones are cracked and the kernels recovered. Nothing is wasted, and the kernel is a product in its own right — used in confectionery and baking, and pressed for oil.

benefits.title: Healthy fats and protein
benefits.text: Mostly unsaturated fat, with protein, magnesium and vitamin E. Close to almonds in composition, and used in much the same way.

benefits.title: Supply tracks our apricot line
benefits.text: The kernels come out of our own apricot processing, so availability follows the apricot harvest rather than a separate crop.

benefits.title: Confectionery and pressing
benefits.text: Whole kernels go into sweets and baking; the rest is pressed for apricot kernel oil, which has its own cosmetic market.

driedPeppers.intro: Capsicum is dried whole in the open air, which concentrates the colour and the heat without the flat taste that hard kiln drying leaves behind. We supply the pods whole rather than ground, so the buyer controls the grind.

benefits.title: Colour and heat concentrated
benefits.text: Drying removes water, not capsaicin or carotenoid pigment. What is left is the same pepper at several times the intensity.

benefits.title: Whole, not ground
benefits.text: Ground pepper loses its aroma on the shelf. Whole pods keep it until they are milled, which is why spice blenders buy them this way.

benefits.title: Vitamin C and carotenoids
benefits.text: Peppers carry more vitamin C by weight than citrus, along with the carotenoids that give them their colour.

driedMelon.intro: Melon is cut into long strips and dried in the sun, then often braided. It is intensely sweet and floral in a way no other dried fruit is, and in Uzbekistan it is served with tea the way others serve biscuits.

benefits.title: Sweetness with nothing added
benefits.text: Drying concentrates the melon's own sugars. Nothing is added — the intensity is simply what is left once the water has gone.

benefits.title: Potassium and beta-carotene
benefits.text: Melon holds its potassium and carotenoid content through drying, and the fibre concentrates along with the sugars.

benefits.title: A speciality, not a commodity
benefits.text: Few origins produce it at export quality. For a buyer looking for something the shelf does not already have, that is the point.

compoteMix.intro: A ready blend of dried apples, apricots, plums, cherries and berries, mixed in the proportions Central Asian compote is actually made in. Buying it as one line means one SKU, one price and one delivery instead of five.

benefits.title: Blended to a fixed recipe
benefits.text: The ratio is held from batch to batch, so the compote your customer makes in March tastes like the one they made in October.

benefits.title: Made from our own lines
benefits.text: Apples, apricots, plums and cherries all come off our own drying floors, which is what keeps the blend consistent.

benefits.title: One SKU instead of five
benefits.text: Fewer purchase orders, fewer part-pallets, and no in-house mixing step at the buyer's end.

sourCherries.intro: Sour cherries are dried whole and slowly, which keeps the skin intact and the acidity high. They behave differently from sweet cherries in a kitchen — the tartness survives baking, which is exactly why bakers buy them.

benefits.title: Anthocyanins and acidity
benefits.text: The deep colour is anthocyanin, the pigment class studied for its antioxidant activity. The acidity comes with it.

benefits.title: Holds up in baking
benefits.text: Sweet cherries flatten out under heat and sugar. Sour cherries do not, which is why they anchor strudel, pie and confectionery fillings.

benefits.title: Covered by our GACC listing
benefits.text: Cherries fall under HS 0813 20, one of the two codes our GACC registration covers, so this line enters China under our own registration.

driedApples.intro: Apples are cored, cut into rings and dried. It is the simplest product we make and the one with the widest use — compote, muesli, baking, and straight snacking.

benefits.title: Fibre, mostly pectin
benefits.text: Apples are unusually high in soluble fibre. Drying concentrates it, and the pectin is what makes them thicken a compote.

benefits.title: Light to ship
benefits.text: At a fraction of the fresh weight, apple rings move a lot of servings per pallet, which keeps freight cost per portion low.

benefits.title: Works in four categories
benefits.text: Compote, breakfast cereal, bakery inclusion and retail snack — one product, four kinds of buyer.
